chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'We make the qalanis (woolen cloaks/garments) and place old cotton in them, and then sell them without specifying to them what is inside.' He said, 'I like for you to specify to them what is inside it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on disclosing the contents of a garment when selling it?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises a companion to explicitly disclose the use of old cotton (*qutn al-atiq*) in garments (*qalanis*) to avoid *gharar* (uncertainty) in trade. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on transparency and preventing deception in commercial transactions, ensuring that buyers are fully aware of the quality and composition of goods they purchase.
